description:
Dispatcher for note operations: create, render, edit, query notes in notes/. With no subcommand it runs `new`.

Subcommands:
  new — create a new note and open it (INTERACTIVE)
  copy [FILTER] — pick a note, copy contents to a new timestamped note (INTERACTIVE)
  strip [FILTER] — pick a note, copy it with the body removed, for templating (INTERACTIVE)
  edit [FILTER] — pick a note, open in the default editor (INTERACTIVE)
  nano [FILTER] — pick a note, open in nano (INTERACTIVE)
  last — open the most recently-created note; the only non-interactive subcommand
  delete [FILTER] — pick a note and permanently delete it (INTERACTIVE, DESTRUCTIVE)
  cat [FILTER] — pick a note and print it to stdout (INTERACTIVE)
  pdf [FILTER] — pick a note, render to PDF + markdown (INTERACTIVE)
  minutes [FILTER] — pick a note, render meeting minutes: TOC plus AGREED/RESOLVED/ACTION summary (INTERACTIVE)
  agenda [FILTER] — pick a note, render a meeting agenda (INTERACTIVE)

Args:
  SUBCOMMAND — optional; defaults to new
  FILTER — optional case-insensitive substring filter applied to the picker list

Body keywords recognised in a note: ACTION: (ingested by `tasks`), TASK: (already ingested; never write by hand), AGREED:, RESOLVED:, !: (callout surfaced in pdf).

Rendering output goes to the export directory, default the user's Downloads folder. pdf, minutes and agenda need pandoc and a LaTeX engine.

Examples:
  ["last"]

Notes:
  Every subcommand except `last` opens an interactive picker that reads a selection from stdin. With no TTY they consume EOF and behave unpredictably instead of failing — never call them. Only ["last"] is safe.
  To create or edit note content without a TTY, capture through `buffer` (add-text, add-action, add-ref) and run `buffer flush`, or edit the note file directly.
  Invoking with no arguments runs `new`, which is interactive — never call with an empty array.
